quality.hardDesign: 결론(자기강화적 되먹임으로 인한 비가역성)이 한 문장에 직접 제시되지 않고, 융해→질량/고도 손실→저지대 위치→융해 가속이라는 여러 문장에 걸친 인과 사슬을 종합해야 도출된다. 오답들은 각각 규모 비교(A, 범위 과장), 세부 메커니즘인 활강 가속만 부각(B, 부분 일치·핵심 결론 누락), 지문에 없는 급진적 결론 날조(D, 텍스트 왜곡)로 설계되어 근거 문장을 정확히 종합하지 않으면 배제하기 어렵다.

problem.passage:
Glacial ice sheets are often likened to "frozen reservoirs" because both store vast quantities of water for gradual release, but this analogy conceals a distinction that hydrologists consider essential. A reservoir behind a dam holds water in a basin whose walls remain structurally intact regardless of how much water is drawn down; the container itself does not disappear when it empties. An ice sheet, however, is simultaneously the container and the contents: it is a solid mass whose own bulk creates the elevation and pressure gradients that regulate how fast meltwater drains toward the sea. When atmospheric warming causes surface melting, the ice does not simply release stored water while leaving its own form untouched. Meltwater often penetrates crevasses and refreezes at the base, and in some regions it instead lubricates the boundary between ice and bedrock, accelerating the glacier's slide toward the ocean; either way, the ice sheet's own mass, and therefore the very structure that slows further melting, is diminished. Once enough of that mass is lost, the remaining ice sits at lower, warmer elevations where melting intensifies, a feedback that does not occur in a rock-walled reservoir, whose basin geometry never changes as it drains. Glaciologists therefore caution that, unlike a reservoir that merely needs new inflow to refill, an ice sheet that has thinned past a certain point may keep losing mass even if temperatures stabilize, only reversing course over millennia rather than seasons, because rebuilding the ice sheet means regenerating the very elevation and mass that regulated its own melt rate in the first place.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

problem.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Ice sheets hold more water than reservoirs do, so their loss threatens global freshwater supplies more severely than a drained reservoir would.
Because meltwater lubricates the base of glaciers, ice sheets slide toward the ocean much faster than reservoirs lose water through evaporation.
Since melting reduces the mass and elevation that once regulated an ice sheet's own melt rate, its decline can become self-reinforcing and far harder to reverse than a reservoir's water loss.
Glaciologists have shown that ice sheets and reservoirs should no longer be compared because meltwater refreezing at the base makes the two systems fundamentally incomparable.
problem.explanation: 지문은 빙상을 '얼어붙은 저수지'에 비유하는 것이 오해를 낳는다고 지적하며, 저수지는 물이 빠져도 그릇(분지 구조)이 그대로지만 빙상은 자신의 질량 자체가 융해 속도를 조절하는 구조이므로, 녹으면서 질량과 고도를 잃으면 더 따뜻한 저지대에 놓여 융해가 가속되는 자기강화적 되먹임이 발생한다고 설명한다. 이어서 이 때문에 온도가 안정되어도 수천 년에 걸쳐서만 회복되는, 저수지와는 다른 비가역성을 강조한다. 따라서 정답은 질량-고도 손실과 자기강화적 되먹임, 회복 난이도를 모두 포괄하는 C이다. A는 저장량 규모 비교에만 그쳐 지문의 핵심인 되먹임과 비가역성을 놓친다. B는 빙하 이동 가속이라는 지문의 세부 사실(원인의 일부)만을 다루고 이를 저수지의 증발 속도와 부적절하게 비교하며, 결론인 질량 손실의 자기강화 및 회복 불가능성을 담지 못한다. D는 지문에 없는 '더 이상 비교할 수 없다'는 주장을 지어낸 오답이다.
